x: "I'm only just getting fit so I'm not taking it seriously", but Gerry North never could resist a challenge and once again, after running the best part of the race with the leading group, turned it on at the end to grab the verdict from Lionel and Laurie.
Laurie's going well .. must fill the scooter tomorrow .... Linda Manning is quite nice looking .... pity Charlie is such a good runner .... a real good dinner tonight ...

Laurie and Leo ran well but both admitted that the London Marathon of the previous week must have slowed them. Nonetheless we turned in our best time for 4 years and had Croydon, Blackheath and Brighton behind us.

Although we didn't send teams to the Vets National Charlie Walker decided to have a go and was rewarded with an excellent 8th place ahead of most of the Southern Vets who had beaten him in the area Championships. If Laurie and Charlie Henn had been running who knows what might have happened in the team results!!!!

If only Laurie hadn't been working! M60 (3 stages): 1, Barnet & Dist. 55:42; 2, Solihull & Small Heath 57:03; 3, Cambridge H 57:14; ... 6, Belgrave (A.Bruce 20:54, P.Newall 19:48, C.Walker 19:35) 60:17. 11 teams completed.
Even with Laurie, the young lad who grabbed my UK 5000m record last year! Still, another set of silver medals behind Barnet again will match those won at Burnley and the Sutton Coldfield Nat.

The sun was low in the sky and there was Laurie's distinctive and diminutive figure, silhouetted for a brief moment as he crested the rise. He was in full flow and I would swear that not once did his shoes touch the ground as he headed for home.

The National Veterans Cross Country Championships were held last March at one of our local venues, Lloyd Park in Croydon, and this provided a fitting occasion for Belgravians to gather in memory of the late Laurie O'Hara who had died almost exactly a year before.
